one_line_description.value: Klaviyo is a data-first marketing platform that helps businesses store customer data and run email, SMS, and other marketing automation.
one_line_description.quote: Klaviyo is a data-first platform designed to make it easy for businesses to know their customers and grow faster.

has_public_api.quote: Create apps and integrations with Klaviyo's API, SDKs and MCP server that help businesses grow.

api_type.quote: you can download the OpenAPI spec the reference is generated from.

api_breadth.value: REST, broad read-write API spanning profiles, events, campaigns, flows, segments, and catalogs; full endpoint reference with per-endpoint limits.
api_breadth.quote: Private API keys can be used to read and write data to your Klaviyo account.

docs_url.quote: Gain the knowledge you need to successfully integrate Klaviyo with your application.

auth_methods.quote: Klaviyo provides 3 methods of authentication including private key authentication and OAuth (used to call server-side APIs) and public key authentication (used to call client-side APIs).

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: The scopes the app needs (for example, `accounts:read profiles:read`).

access_model.quote: Navigate to your account’s Settings page and select API keys. Under the Private API Keys section, select Create Private API Key.

access_notes.value: Private API keys and OAuth apps are self-serve from the Klaviyo account, but only Owner/Admin/Manager roles can create them; OAuth is required for App Marketplace listing and app review. Klaviyo's MCP server is also restricted to Owner/Admin/Manager roles. Plan-tier gating for production use could not be confirmed because the full pricing page text was not in the evidence set.
access_notes.quote: Note that only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps in Klaviyo.

rate_limits.value: Per-account fixed-window limiting with two windows: burst (1-second) and steady (1-minute), applied to all new API endpoints; HTTP 429 when exceeded; per-endpoint numeric limits listed in the API reference; OAuth apps get their own quota per installed app instance.
rate_limits.quote: All new API endpoints are rate limited on a per-account basis, and use a fixed-window rate limiting algorithm with two distinct windows: burst (1-second window) and steady (1-minute window).

webhooks.quote: If you are using a Klaviyo webhook, custom integration, or API implementation, it is important to be aware of the limits on the events you send into Klaviyo.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: Create a test account: Learn how to create a sandbox account that is linked to your production account login. Test your code end-to-end.

sdk_languages.quote: Klaviyo offers SDKs for server-side languages (Python, PHP, Ruby, Node) and mobile platforms (iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter).

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Date-based API revisions passed via a `revision` header (e.g., 2026-10-15); beta APIs require a `.pre` revision header and are subject to change; Klaviyo publishes an API versioning and deprecation policy and a changelog per API revision.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: A beta revision header (2026-10-15.pre) is required to use our beta APIs.

verdict_reason: Klaviyo publishes a full public REST API reference plus official SDKs for Python, PHP, Ruby, Node, and mobile platforms, with self-serve private API keys generated in account settings and OAuth for partner apps. Access requires no sales contact or partner approval for basic credentials, only an Owner/Admin/Manager role on the account. The API is broad and read-write, and Klaviyo even operates its own MCP server at https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp.
open_questions: Free-tier/plan gating for API credentials could not be confirmed because only a search snippet of https://www.klaviyo.com/pricing was available, not the full page text; confirm whether any plan level blocks API key creation.

Webhooks evidence was limited to a single passing mention in the rate-limits page; the dedicated webhook pages appeared only as snippets, and one snippet says only Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners can manage webhooks via the Webhooks API — verify this gating.
Specific numeric rate limits (burst/steady requests per window) are per-endpoint in the API reference and were not enumerated in the fetched pages.
No community/third-party MCP servers were found in the provided evidence (GitHub and MCP registry checks returned nothing), so the null is a search-coverage gap rather than proof none exist.
Whether OAuth app creation requires a paid Klaviyo plan or Klaviyo app-partner status was not explicitly stated in the fetched pages.
